first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) plus a related activation-messaging memory (memory_91) converge on simplifying/shortening onboarding as a durable, low-risk lever for exactly these metrics—directly addressing the internal decline rather than reacting to the competitor. Promotional pricing (memory_73) looks superficially attractive given the competitor's pricing move, but that memory is explicitly flagged as having pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its acquisition/revenue lift numbers are suspect and risk attracting low-LTV, price-sensitive accounts that undermine sustainable qualified revenue—exactly the segment the competitor is fighting over. I'm spending verification budget on memory_73 to check whether the pooling issue invalidates or merely weakens the promotional-pricing case (in case it should be reconsidered next cycle), and on memory_31 since it's the primary basis for this week's action and confirming its original effect size/duration reduces risk of over-committing based on a stale or narrow signal. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are valuable but don't address the acute, worsening onboarding/activation metrics this week, and only one experiment slot is available. I'm running this as a standard (not broad) experiment to preserve optionality and re-test given the current volatile competitive environment.
